title: Transactional rollout locks and deadline guards for SDK rollout APIs
creator: Leila Moradi
description: Add transactional locking and deadline/lease guards to the rollout control-plane API and SDK helpers to ensure safe, idempotent canary rollouts, A/B traffic splits, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket implements a lock+lease primitive on the rollout resource so concurrent clients (CLI/SDK/webhooks/orchestration services) cannot issue conflicting state transitions. It also adds a deadline guard so long-held locks are auto-expired and reconciled by the reconciler rather than blocking traffic management indefinitely. The goal is to avoid duplicate canary activations, partially-applied traffic splits, and stuck rollouts during control-plane failover or slow clients.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes start_rollout_transaction(idempotency_token, target_model, policy) that acquires a rollout lease and returns a lease_id and expiration
Rollout API honors 'Idempotency-Token' header and returns 2xx for duplicate requests when transaction already applied
Leases automatically expire after configured TTL and the reconciler detects and recovers expired leases within 30s
Concurrent clients attempting conflicting transitions receive 409 with a suggested retry-after and lease_owner metadata
Integration tests simulate network partitions and verify no more than one active canary exposure for a given model+route key
tasks: Design: finalize lock model and lease semantics with SRE and product (2d)
API: add /rollouts/{id}/transactions endpoint (POST/GET/DELETE) and Idempotency-Token header handling (3d)
SDK: implement client helpers (start, refresh_lease, commit, abort) and automatic retry/backoff (3d)
Reconciler: detect expired leases and run safe rollback/reconciliation flow (3d)
E2E tests: develop chaos tests that kill control-plane leader during an active transaction (2d)
Docs + runbook: update runbook with steps to diagnose stuck leases (1d)
decisions: Use optimistic lease with TTL instead of hard mutex to avoid cross-region blocking
IdempotencyToken will be orthogonal to lease_id: token guarantees single commit semantics for client retries; lease_id controls concurrent writers
Lease TTL default set to 60s with ability to configure per-organization via rollout policy
Conflicting changes return 409 with 'Retry-After' and 'Lease-Owner' headers to help SDK surface guidance
implementation_notes: Store lease metadata in rollout's primary storage row with last_lease_acquired_at, lease_owner_id, lease_expires_at to keep read path cheap
Use CAS/conditional write in datastore to acquire lease; fallback path returns current lease metadata
Reconciler periodically scans rollouts with lease_expires_at < now() - grace_window to ensure there is no half-applied state
SDK will surface a high-level convenience API and a low-level lease API for advanced users (e.g., orchestration systems)
Avoid long synchronous waits in HTTP handlers: return 202 Accepted with lease payload and let client poll/subscribe to rollout status via events/webhooks
api_contract_proposal: POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/transactions - body: {idempotency_token, target_model, traffic_plan, policy}, returns {transaction_id, lease_id, lease_expires_at}
DELETE /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/transactions/{transaction_id} - abort (requires lease ownership or admin scope)
HTTP semantics: duplicate POSTs with same Idempotency-Token return the original transaction if it succeeded; conflicting active leases return 409
client_helpers: start_rollout_transaction(rollout_id, target_model, traffic_plan, idempotency_token) -> {transaction_id, lease_id, expires_at}
refresh_lease(rollout_id, lease_id) -> extends lease; SDK does exponential backoff on transient errors
commit_transaction(transaction_id, lease_id) -> finalizes traffic changes; verifies lease ownership
abort_transaction(transaction_id, lease_id) -> safe abort and rollback of partial changes
automatic_backoff_and_resume: helper that implements jittered retries based on Retry-After header
local_transaction_cache in SDK to dedupe duplicate in-process requests across multiple threads/processes
test_plan: Unit tests for API idempotency logic (happy path / duplicate / conflict)
Integration tests: SDK + API: start -> commit -> verify traffic exposed to new model variant
Chaos test: simulate control-plane leader restart while lease held, ensure reconciler recovers and no double-apply
Load test: 500 concurrent start_rollout requests across 50 different rollouts to confirm 409 rate and latencies
Security test: ensure abort requires same lease owner or admin scope (RBAC checks)
rollout_runbook: How to identify stuck lease: search rollouts where lease_expires_at > now() + configured_buffer and status != terminal
Manual release: curl DELETE /v1/rollouts/{id}/transactions/{tx} with admin token to force-release lease
Reconciler recovery: steps to run reconciler job ad-hoc and inspect logs for recovery decisions
Customer impact assessment: check per-route metrics (exposure, errors, latency) before and after forced release
blockers: Awaiting storage schema migration for lease fields (migration ticket ENG-61820)
Open question about cross-region lease arbitration (SRE design review scheduled)
Need a short RFC approval on default TTL values from product/security
